notes: Check batch of four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so the opus tier is unavailable in per_rule. Each result.json records head e83b4f2 with uncommitted changes (the brief named 9fde8f6); their skill_hash (ea8a7b8c...) equals the hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/ folder computed with evals/tools/common.py folder_hash, and each transcript contains the new do: rule's last sentence. All four have rc 0 and the expected model_id, and read SKILL.md and no reference file, which meets Expected reads. In the scratch folder, with Decimal 2.3.0 built from the local Hex cache on the code path, all four pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with --warnings-as-errors; the doctests pass (haiku-2 1, sonnet-1 1, sonnet-2 2; haiku-1 has none). A probe gives correct per-currency totals, UTC last-order dates and top-customer order for a mixed sample, empty results for [], and {:error, reason} from all four for a bad amount, trailing text, an unknown status and a missing key. Haiku-2 returns last_order_at as a DateTime where the prompt asks for a date, and its field/2 passes non-string values on, so a non-string amount raises FunctionClauseError in Decimal.parse/1; CSV values are strings, so this is not listed. The erl_crash.dump in skill-sonnet-2 came from the run's own `elixir orders.ex 2>&1 | head` check and is not part of its output.

New rule, graded against its text: "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md lines 334-350), decided by line 336. Violating runs out of 4 per sentence: `do:` on a body of more than one expression or several steps 0; a `case`, `with` or comment under `do:` 0; short `do:` clauses and a block clause in one function not set apart by a blank line 0 (no run has a function that mixes the two forms); several block clauses mixed with `do:` clauses 0 (none written); a one-liner wrapped onto a `do:` line of its own 0 (no `do:` line wraps). Every `do:` in the batch is a one-expression parse_status/1 clause (haiku-1 lines 99-102, haiku-2 87-90, sonnet-1 172-175, sonnet-2 140-143) or haiku-2's predicate completed?/1 (line 132), and every multi-step body, case and with is in a block, so all four are clean. Not counted, since the miss list for this round does not include it: haiku-2 writes two one-expression bodies as blocks (customer_entry/1, lines 99-101, and customer_summary/1, lines 103-105), which the first sentence would place on `do:`.

Rule reworded before the previous check batch, graded to that batch's standard: "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function", decided by "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 118) and the public-function sentence on line 150. Violating runs out of 4: one-step `with` 0 (all four write build/1's single parse call as a case with `{:error, _reason} = error -> error`: haiku-1 line 41, haiku-2 line 30, sonnet-1 line 71, sonnet-2 line 74); a `case` nested in a `with` body 0; `else` 0. All four chain lookups and parses in one eight-step with (haiku-1 lines 57-64, haiku-2 46-53, sonnet-1 130-137, sonnet-2 90-97). The previous check batch also had 0 of 4; the second sweep had 2 of 5.

Unchanged rule, graded to the second sweep's standard: "Use the `Enum` or `Map` function made for the job", decided by the table row ending "a `reduce` that reads and writes one key per element is these two written by hand" (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 223). Hand-written per-key fold: 0 of 4 (previous check batch 0 of 4, second sweep 1 of 5). All four group customers with Enum.group_by/2 and Map.new/2 and each customer's completed amounts with Enum.group_by/3 then Map.new/2 (haiku-1 lines 128-129, haiku-2 110-111, sonnet-1 100-101, sonnet-2 173-174). Sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 count completed orders with Enum.frequencies_by/2 (lines 109, 187); haiku-1 counts the filtered list that also feeds the totals with Enum.count/1 (line 121) and haiku-2 uses Enum.count/2 per group (line 125), both held clean as before. The Decimal sums with Enum.reduce are reductions no table row replaces, and the reduce_while loops build lists.

Captures rule, reworded before the previous check batch, graded to that batch's standard, decided by "so is a capture that uses `&1` and `&2` for one operator or one call, such as `&(&1 + &2)` or `&Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2)`. When the body does more than one call, or would need `&3`, write `fn` with named arguments." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 360). Violating runs: 0 of 4 (previous check batch 0 of 4). Unlike the previous batch, where three runs wrote &Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2), all four now pull the amounts out with Enum.group_by/3 and sum with &Decimal.add/2 (haiku-1 line 130, haiku-2 112, sonnet-1 102, sonnet-2 175), so the &2 sentence is not tested here. Sonnet-2's &DateTime.to_date(&1.placed_at) (line 181) is one call, held clean. No capture has more than one call or &3; every fn destructures a tuple or names the reduce_while arguments around a case.

Unchanged rule, graded to the earlier standard: Naming. Violating runs per sentence, out of 4: modules CamelCase and snake_case 0; top-level namespace 0; boolean functions end in ? 0 (haiku-2's completed?/1; the others define none); get/fetch 0 (haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 name the checking lookup string_field/2 and haiku-2 names its plain lookup field/2, so no function is named get or fetch; the previous batch had 1 of 4, haiku-2's fetch_field/2); size/length 0; ignored values 0; domain variable names 0 (sonnet-1's result, line 115, held to the earlier standard, which passed result).

Other unchanged rules follow the earlier standard. All four match Decimal.parse/1's {amount, ""}, {_amount, _rest} and :error, so no catch-all is listed this time. Haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 parse into an Order struct with @type t; haiku-2 parses into atom-keyed maps (line 55), not listed, as the second sweep did not list atom-keyed maps. Only haiku-1's build/1 @doc lacks ## Examples, listed under the Comments rule. reduce_while piped into case is gone; sonnet-1 binds the reduce_while result and matches it with case (lines 115-126), not listed.
